# Copilot instructions

## Build and test

- Build the solution: `dotnet build Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.slnx`
- Run the test suite: `dotnet test tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests.csproj`
- Run one test: `dotnet test tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~WorkItemServiceTests.Accept_Hierarchy_CreatesLabelledSubIssuesAndOnlyAssignsTheStory"`
- Restore the local EF tool before using it: `dotnet tool restore`
- Set `ConnectionStrings__Database` in the shell before using EF tools (use the connection string from your local development settings).
- Add a migration: `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.DataAccess.Sql --output-dir Migrations`
- Check the migration snapshot: `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes --project src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.DataAccess.Sql`
- Azure deployment: `.github\workflows\release.yml` builds and tests on pushes and pull requests to `main`. On every push to `main`, it applies an EF migrations bundle to Azure SQL and deploys the web app to App Service and `Sync` to the Flex Consumption Function App `softwarefactory-sync`. One-time OIDC setup is in `scripts\setup-azure-github.ps1`; see `docs\azure-deployment.md`.

The app targets .NET 10. Development startup applies EF migrations automatically and uses the LocalDB connection string in `appsettings.Development.json`; other environments must supply `ConnectionStrings:Database`. `appsettings.Development.json` is gitignored, is not published and holds personal settings such as `OpenAI:ApiKey`; `README.md` shows its shape (keep that in sync when adding settings). Development startup migrates whatever database that file points at, so keep it on a local database.
- `SqlServerStoreTests` run against a real SQL Server (a new database per test, built by the migrations): LocalDB on Windows, or the connection string (without database) in `DGHSF_TEST_SQL_SERVER`, which CI sets to a SQL Server service container; they are skipped when neither is available. Use them for what the InMemory provider doesn't enforce (unique indexes, restricted foreign keys, collation, concurrency tokens).
- CI builds with `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`, so fix analyzer warnings (including in tests) instead of leaving them.

## Architecture

- Project references flow from `Web` to `Application`, and from `Application` to `DataAccess.Sql` and `Agents`. All libraries share `Contracts`, which has no application or infrastructure dependencies. Keep Web free of EF and Agent Framework types.
- `Application/Features` contains MediatR commands, queries, handlers and FluentValidation validators grouped by feature, one type per file in `Commands`, `Queries` and `Validators` subfolders (e.g. `WorkItems/Queries/GetWorkItemQuery.cs` and `GetWorkItemQueryHandler.cs`); these keep the feature namespace. Requests and responses wrap records from `Contracts`; collection responses wrap `CollectionResult<T>`. UI-facing application services dispatch through MediatR, whose validation pipeline runs before handlers and throws `ValidationFailedException` (Contracts). Domain rules that refuse an operation (in stores, workflows and services) throw `DomainRuleException` (Contracts) with a message for the user; UI catch filters show those two (and `PersistenceException`, GitHub errors) and let `InvalidOperationException` surface as a bug. Every request with a repository name validates it with `ValidRepositoryFullName()` (`Application/Common/RepositoryNameRules`), because the name goes into GitHub API URLs.
- `DataAccess.Sql` owns EF entities, DTO mapping, stores, `AppDbContext`, migrations and the design-time factory. Stores live in `Stores` behind interfaces (`IWorkItemStore`, ...) that are registered and injected through DI. Entity configuration lives in `Configuration`, one `ModelBuilder` extension per entity, called from `OnModelCreating`. Stores use `IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>` and dispose a context per operation. DTOs are separate records, not EF entities. Every entity derives from `Entity`: `Id` (`Guid`, generated by the application) is the nonclustered primary key that foreign keys, contracts and URLs use, and `SysId` (`int` identity) is a clustered alternate key that stays inside `DataAccess.Sql` (`EntityKeysConfiguration`); sort on `SysId` for insertion order, never on `Id`. Existing migration IDs are preserved.
- `Agents` owns Microsoft Agent Framework agents, sessions, streaming and AI form tools. `Application.Features.Assistant` exposes framework-free conversations and tool factories to Web. Contract records are mutable where form binding requires it; use `Copy()` or `with` for editable copies.
- This is a .NET 10 Blazor app using Interactive Server rendering without prerendering for interactive routes. GitHub OAuth is single-user: `Program.cs` enforces the configured allowed login and keeps the access token in the server-side authentication ticket, which `SqlTicketStore` encrypts with data protection and stores in the SQL `AuthSessions` table (through `AuthSessionService`), so sign-ins survive restarts and deployments; the cookie only holds a random session key. GitHub API calls get the token from the `GitHubClaims.AccessToken` claim through `AuthenticationStateProvider`.
- The app operates on one selected repository per Blazor circuit. `RepositoryContext` restores and stores the selection in protected browser local storage, and `MainLayout` then refreshes it from GitHub (`RefreshAsync`; the stored copy is kept when GitHub can't be reached); `MainLayout` requires a selection and keys the page body by repository full name so switching repositories recreates the page. Pages marked `[RepositoryIndependent]` (detected through the `RouteData` cascaded from `Routes.razor`) render without a selection, e.g. the agent template pages.
- Repository selection and restored selections update SQL `RepositoryAccesses` through `RepositoryHistoryService`. The picker loads the five most recent names/access times independently of GitHub's full repository list and fetches a recent repository directly when selected before that list finishes.
- Agent templates (`AgentTemplateService`) are stored in SQL Server as full agent file content, are shared across repositories, and are applied to one or more repositories through the application workflow and `GitHubApiClient`. `AgentEditor` and `AgentTemplateEditor` share the `Components/Shared/AgentForm.razor` form.
- Repository-backed features should use `RepositoryContext.Current` and pass the repository full name through application service operations. Work items are scoped by repository; the managed AI model catalog, agent templates and work item templates are shared across repositories.
- `Sync` is an isolated-worker Azure Function app that references only `Application` (through `AddSoftwareFactory`). `WorkItemSyncFunction` runs on the CRON expression in the `WorkItemSyncSchedule` app setting and calls `WorkItemSyncService`, which refreshes every item with `WorkItem.HasIssue` (also closed ones, so a reopened issue moves back) of every repository in `IRepositoryStore.GetAllAsync` through `WorkItemService.RefreshAsync`. Nobody is signed in when the timer fires, so its `IGitHubTokenProvider` returns `GitHub:SyncToken` from configuration. A failure of one item or repository is reported in `WorkItemSyncResult` and logged; a refused token or reached rate limit throws, because every other request would fail too. `local.settings.json` is gitignored; `README.md` shows its shape.
- Work items (epics, features, user stories, bugs and tasks) share one model: `WorkItem` with a `WorkItemType`, stored in the `WorkItems` table with a self-referencing `ParentId`; templates are `WorkItemTemplate` rows per type. `WorkItemTypeRules` (Contracts) holds the label, label color, names and hierarchy per type: a feature needs an epic parent, a story needs a feature parent, bugs and tasks are standalone or part of an epic, feature or story. Only stories, bugs and tasks are assigned to the Copilot cloud agent; the store clears assignment settings for epics and features. `WorkItemStore` enforces the hierarchy and refuses to delete items with children. `WorkItemWorkflow` creates the labelled issue (creating the label when missing), makes it a sub-issue of the parent's issue and makes the issues of already accepted children its sub-issues (the sub-issues API needs GitHub's issue id, stored as `IssueId`). Accepting first claims the draft (`AcceptStartedAt`, a concurrency token like `Status`; a claim expires after `WorkItemWorkflow.AcceptClaimTimeout`) so concurrent accepts can't both create an issue. When an attempt failed after GitHub may have created the issue (not for a 4xx refusal), `AcceptIssueSince` remembers when it started and the next attempt first looks for the issue with the item's marker among the label's issues updated since then (`FindIssueByMarkerAsync`), reusing it instead of creating a duplicate. The marker (`WorkItemWorkflow.Marker`, `<!-- dghsf:label:id:created-ms -->`) includes the creation time, so items of different databases never share one.
- Accepted items (`WorkItem.HasIssue`) have a Refresh from GitHub button on the list and on the editor. `WorkItemWorkflow.RefreshFromIssueAsync` (MediatR `RefreshWorkItemCommand`) reads the issue and `IWorkItemStore.ApplyIssueAsync` stores its title, body without the marker, id and URL, and the status that follows from it: closed is Done (labeled Closed in the UI); open is In progress when Copilot is assigned (only for assignable types), otherwise Accepted. So a reopened or unassigned issue moves back. It only reads from GitHub, `UpdatedAt` changes only when something differed, and the editor keeps unsaved assignment settings.
- The work item pages (`WorkItems`, `WorkItemEditor`, `WorkItemTemplates`, `WorkItemTemplateEditor`) each serve all types through one `@page` per type; `WorkItemRoutes` maps types to URLs (`/epics`, `/features`, `/stories`, `/bugs`, `/tasks`, `/{label}-templates`) and reads the type from the URL. The pages take the cascaded `RouteData` so navigating between types (same component) reloads them. That cascade reaches the current page before its own parameters are updated, so a page combining the URL's type with its `Id` first checks `WorkItemRoutes.IsOutOfStep`; without that check it sees the new URL with the old id.
- The overview page shows `RepositoryInfographic` (Shared): whether the Copilot instructions file exists, the number of custom agents (from the directory listing with `AgentCatalog.IsAgentFile`, without reading every file) and per work item type the `WorkItemCounts` from one `GROUP BY` in `IWorkItemStore.GetCountsAsync`. The counts are by current status, so every item is in exactly one: draft, accepted (Accepted or In progress) or closed (Done). Each part fails on its own, so GitHub being unreachable doesn't hide the counts.
- Below it, `CopilotActivityInfographic` and `CopilotBillingInfographic` (Shared) show live GitHub data; nothing is stored in SQL. Activity: the selected repository's Copilot pull request activity over the last 28 days, from GitHub's Copilot usage metrics `orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics/reports/repos-1-day` report (only for organization-owned repositories, `GitHubOwner.IsOrganization`; needs an organization owner or the View Organization Copilot Metrics permission, the usage metrics policy and the `read:org` OAuth scope). There is no multi-day repository report, so `GetCopilotRepositoryMetricsQueryHandler` requests one report per day (4 at a time). Each report returns signed links to NDJSON files, which `GitHubApiClient` downloads **without** the GitHub token, and the handler caches each day's rows per organization in `IMemoryCache`. A 404 for one of the last 3 days counts as not published yet; an older 404 is an access problem. GitHub has no usage metrics for personal accounts, so for a personal repository `GetCopilotPullRequestActivityQueryHandler` works out the same period from the pull requests list (sorted by update time, so paging stops at the first one updated before the period) and each pull request's reviews. Authors and reviewers are Copilot when `GitHubOwner.IsCopilot` (a Bot whose login contains "copilot"), and each pull request counts once, on the day of its first Copilot review. It sets `CopilotRepositoryMetrics.FromPullRequests`; then the component hides the review comment stat and severity table and says where the numbers come from. The result is cached for 10 minutes per repository. Don't use the search API for this: its secondary rate limit trips after a few quick requests. Billing: this month's (UTC) premium request and AI credit usage of the repository owner (`organizations/{org}/...` or `users/{login}/settings/billing/{premium_request|ai_credit}/usage`), per model. The user endpoints only accept the full `user` OAuth scope (hence `user` instead of `read:user` at sign-in) and answer 404 without it; the organization endpoints accept `repo` and need an organization owner or billing manager. The two reports fail independently. Billing amounts are shown in US dollars, as GitHub bills them, not with `AiModel.FormatPrice`. These endpoints are sent with `X-GitHub-Api-Version` `GitHubApiClient.UsageApiVersion`; the rest of the client keeps the default version.
- Custom agent profiles live in each repository's `.github/agents` directory and are read or committed through `GitHubApiClient`. `AgentFileSerializer` preserves unedited YAML frontmatter keys and their order; retain that behavior when changing agent-file editing.
- `/copilot-instructions` (`CopilotInstructions.razor`) edits the selected repository's `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (`CopilotInstructionsFile` in Contracts) in `MarkdownEditor` with `RawMarkdown` (no WYSIWYG round trip, so existing Markdown isn't reformatted) and commits it directly to the default branch through `GitHubService.PutFileAsync` (no sha when the file doesn't exist yet). Its Copilot (`CopilotInstructionsFormTools`) can list and read repository files (read-only, long files are cut off) to write concrete instructions, and replaces the editor content; the user saves.
- `/copilot-code-review` (`CopilotCodeReview.razor`) reads and changes the selected repository's Copilot code review settings live through `repos/{owner}/{repo}/copilot/code-review/settings`; nothing is stored in SQL. Every control sends a `PATCH` with only its own setting and shows the settings GitHub returns. GitHub's API offers review effort, severity filter, custom instructions and MCP, but not maximum review effort or approvals, and requires repository administrator access.
- DGHSF's internal agents use the singleton `AssistantAgentFactory` in `Agents` and the `OpenAI` config section (`Endpoint`, `Model`, `ApiKey`; unconfigured means the chat shows a setup hint). The fixed set of agents and their default system prompts live in `InternalAgentDefaults` (keys in Contracts `InternalAgentKeys`): one Copilot per work item type, per work item template type, for agents, for agent templates and for the Copilot instructions file, plus the background agents Model Selector, Chat Suggestions, Description Writer and Work Item Breakdown. They are stored in the `InternalAgents` table (seeded at startup through `SeedApplicationDataAsync` and whenever the list is loaded; seeding adds missing agents and refreshes name/description but keeps edited prompts and the enabled flag). `InternalAgentRegistry` merges the stored prompt with the defaults; `/internal-agents` edits the prompt, enables/disables and resets an agent. Internal agents are global, not per repository. Every internal agent links to a row of the internal model catalog (`InternalModel`, `/internal-models`: the Microsoft Foundry model or deployment name that is sent to the endpoint, a required one-line `Label` shown when choosing a model, a longer description and EUR per 1M input/output tokens, plus an optional cached input price that falls back to the input price; unrelated to the GitHub-facing `AiModel` catalog), chosen in a select (`AssistantAgentFactory` creates a client per model). A model can be marked `IsFlagship` (any number) and `IsDefault` (at most one, because `InternalModelStore.SaveAsync` clears the previous default in the same save). Seeding links newly added agents to the default model and leaves existing ones alone. An agent without a link uses `OpenAI:Model`. The editor prefills a Copilot's empty model with the default model, or else the catalog entry named like `OpenAI:Model`, prefills a background agent's empty model with the default until that agent is first saved, requires a model for Copilots (optional for background agents) and only enables Save once a new or changed model has passed its Test (`InternalAgentService.TestModelAsync` sends a real request). Resetting restores only the prompt. A model in use can't be deleted.
- All prices and costs are shown in euro with 3 decimals through `AiModel.FormatPrice`. That is display only: more decimals are stored and used to calculate, and `ModelPricingScraper` copies GitHub's US dollar amounts without converting them.
- Token spend: `UsageTrackingChatClient` sits below the agent's function invocation loop, so every model request (each round trip of a tool-using turn, streaming or not) reports its `UsageDetails` through `IAgentUsageRecorder`; so does a model Test on the editor, which counts towards that agent at the price of the tested model. `IInternalAgentStore.RecordUsageAsync` prices the request from the catalog at that moment and, in one save, adds an `InternalAgentUsages` row (a copy of the model name, prices and costs, no foreign key to the model) and adds to the running totals on `InternalAgents`, so later price changes don't affect past costs. Reasoning tokens are stored and shown for information only: they are part of the output tokens and already in the output cost, so never charge them separately. Every row has an `InternalAgentUsageSource` (an enum with descriptions, stored by name): the background agents and the model Test pass their own, and `InternalAgentUsageSources.ForCopilot` maps a Copilot's key to its chat, so a new agent needs a new member there. `UsageTiles` and `UsageRequestsTable` (Shared) are used on both the agent's page and `/internal-agents`, which adds up the running totals and lists the latest requests of all agents. `RequestCount` is a concurrency token and the store retries when simultaneous requests collide. An unknown model is recorded with its tokens at no cost, and failing to record is logged and never breaks the agent. Copilot prompts are edited in `MarkdownEditor` with `RawMarkdown`, because a WYSIWYG round trip would reformat them and make them differ from the default; background agent prompts stay plain text.
- Copilot chats: Web uses `AssistantChat` with a `CopilotKey` and tools from `AssistantForms.ForAgent` / `ForWorkItem` / `ForWorkItemTemplate`. Form tools read and update state through an `onUi` callback (`InvokeAsync` + `StateHasChanged`) and expose a form snapshot. Tools only change the form; the user saves. The work item Copilots have no section structure in their prompts: `WorkItemFormTools` sends the selected template and a copy of the current title and description along with every user message (`AssistantTools.RequestContext`) and offers `get_selected_template`; the template isn't stored on the item, so a saved draft has none selected. Replies are rendered as Markdown by `ChatMarkdown`, which treats model output as untrusted (prompt injection): raw HTML is escaped, only http(s)/mailto links are kept and images become links; keep it that way. A disabled Copilot hides its chat. Before a conversation starts, `AssistantChat` asks the Chat Suggestions agent (`BackgroundAgents.SuggestPromptsAsync`, with the form snapshot) for 3 chips; the page's static suggestions are the fallback. On the work item editors the chips are written again (`AssistantChat.RefreshSuggestions`) when the title or description loses focus after a change (`MarkdownEditor.OnBlur`), not per keystroke; during a conversation no chips are shown, so nothing is refreshed.
- Background agents (`BackgroundAgents`) use structured output (`RunAsync<T>`), so edited prompts can't break the result format. `WorkItemModelSelector` lets the Model Selector suggest an enabled managed model for a story, bug or task (`WorkItemService.SelectModelAsync`; nothing is saved). The work item editor debounces it: 3 seconds after the last description change (typed or filled in by the Copilot) it shows the suggestion as a chip under the model picker, and clicking the chip applies it. It also suggests once, without delay, when an existing draft with a description is opened; other fields and new items (template skeletons) don't trigger it. The model is never picked automatically: "Auto" stays Copilot's automatic model selection.
- `MarkdownEditor` and `MarkdownViewer` create Toast UI editors and viewers in `MarkdownEditor.razor.js` through Toast UI's public API (contract covered by `MarkdownEditorTests`); the ToastUIEditor package is only used for the Toast UI script and stylesheet it ships (imported by path, so its version is pinned exactly), not for its Blazor components. The editor's `addImageBlobHook` replaces Toast UI's base64 images. With `AllowImages` (work item and work item template editors) and the `ImageUploads` config section set, images stream over the circuit to `ImageUploadService`, which validates the format by signature and stores them under a random name in a public Azure blob container (`IImageStorage`); otherwise images are refused.
- Title fields (work item title, template title example) are `DictationTextField`s: a `MudTextField` with a microphone end adornment (none when read-only). It is hidden unless the `Speech` config section (`SpeechOptions`: `Region`, `ApiKey`, optional `Endpoint`, `Language` with up to four comma-separated locales for language detection) is set. `SpeechService.GetTokenAsync` (MediatR `GetSpeechTokenQuery`) has `AzureSpeechTokenIssuer` exchange the key for a 10-minute Azure AI Speech token, reused until 2 minutes before it expires. `wwwroot/js/dictation.js` then recognizes one utterance in the browser with the Speech SDK for JavaScript, which is vendored in `wwwroot/lib/microsoft-cognitiveservices-speech-sdk-<version>` (the path has the version; update it with the files). The key never goes to the browser. The text is trimmed and loses its closing period before it replaces the field.
- Description editors (work item description, template skeleton) pass a `DescriptionDictation` to `MarkdownEditor`, which then shows a microphone at the top right, next to its `Header` (the pages pass their heading and help text). It listens continuously (`recognizeContinuous` in `dictation.js`, with interim text shown under the editor and the token renewed every minute through `GetSpeechToken`) until the microphone is clicked again or Done, at most 10 minutes. `SpeechService.WriteDescriptionAsync` (MediatR `WriteDictatedDescriptionQuery`) then lets the Description Writer background agent merge the transcript into the current description, following the template skeleton; when that agent is disabled, unconfigured or fails, the transcript is appended as a new paragraph. The result replaces the description, with Undo in the snackbar.
- Work item templates have an `IsDefault` flag: at most one per type, because `WorkItemTemplateStore.SaveAsync` clears the previous default in the same save. `WorkItemTemplate.Proposed` picks the default, or else the first alphabetically; new items and generated children both use it.
- Child generation: `WorkItemTypeRules.GeneratedChildType` maps epic to feature, feature to story and story to task. The editor's Generate button (bottom of the page, in the children box; hidden when the Work Item Breakdown agent is disabled or not configured) saves the item and opens `WorkItemChildGenerator` (`/{plural}/{id}/generate`). That page runs the agent (`BackgroundAgents.GenerateChildrenAsync`, MediatR `GenerateChildWorkItemsQuery`) with the parent, the proposed template and the existing children's titles; nothing is stored. The selected proposals are saved as drafts in one transaction (`SaveGeneratedWorkItemsCommand`, `IWorkItemStore.AddGeneratedChildrenAsync`). The agent's output is cleaned in `BackgroundAgents` (blank and duplicate titles dropped, lengths and `GeneratedWorkItem.MaxPerRun` enforced).
- Write extension methods with C# 14 `extension(...)` blocks.
- Use block bodies (`{ ... }`) for methods, constructors, operators and local functions, also in Razor `@code` blocks; expression bodies only where a block is not possible. `.editorconfig` enforces this for C# files.
- UI pages are Razor components using MudBlazor. Tests use xUnit and bUnit in `tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests`.
- Every page in the main layout starts with `PageBreadcrumbs`: the trail from the overview and a back arrow to the page one level up (`BackHref` overrides it). Page actions go in a row of text buttons between the title and the first box, as on the overview pages; detail pages have no Cancel, because the back arrow does that. Pages editing something stored have a Reset that confirms, loads the stored version again without setting `_loading` (which would tear down the form and its Copilot conversation), and isn't shown on new items.

## Repository guidance

`README.md` describes the app, local setup (settings, tests) and deployment for people; this file holds the details for Copilot. `IDEAS.md` includes both implemented features and roadmap items; confirm behavior in the source before treating planned features as available.
